name: instinct-msp-intelligence
description: Research managed service providers (MSPs): company profiles, detected technology vendors, operating-maturity scores, reputation, hiring, security posture, and market counts. Read-only, company-level business data.

interface.longDescription:
Instinct MSP Intelligence lets you research managed service providers (MSPs) and IT resellers that offer managed services across the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Ireland, Australia, and New Zealand.

Look up a company by its website to see its profile, the managed services it offers, the technology vendors detected in use, its public ratings on Google Maps, Glassdoor, and Indeed, hiring and social media activity, email and domain security setup, website performance and search rankings, ownership structure, and what has changed recently. The Fox Crow Maturity Level (FCML) score rates how established a company's operations appear from public signals, and you can see the signals behind each score.

For market research, count companies by location, size, services, vendors, maturity, or recent activity, and compare a company with its peers.

All tools are read-only. Results describe companies, not people: the app returns no personal contact information. Some results, such as revenue estimates and security findings, are modeled or inferred from public data and are labeled as such. Sign in with an Instinct account to use the app.
capabilities: Count MSPs by location, size, services, vendors, maturity, or recent activity
Look up a company by its website and see whether it is classified as an MSP
See a company's firmographic profile: focus, size, locations, and social links
Break down a company's Fox Crow Maturity Level score into its underlying signals
See the technology vendors detected at a company (RMM, PSA, security, backup)
Read a company's ratings and review counts on Google Maps, Glassdoor, and Indeed
See current job postings and hiring activity
Check email and domain security: SPF, DMARC, DKIM, TLS, and providers
See externally visible security exposure and known-exploited vulnerabilities
Rank a company against peers in its state, size class, or service area
See what changed recently: reviews, followers, jobs, website edits, blog posts
Identify ownership: independent, private-equity roll-up, corporate group, or franchise
defaultPrompt: How many MSPs are there in each US state?
What is simpsoncomputing.com's maturity score, and which signals drive it?
Which technology vendors have been detected at simpsoncomputing.com?

positive.prompt: How many MSPs are there in each US state?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls count_companies with group_by set to state and returns a total plus a per-state breakdown. Only counts are returned, never company names; any state with fewer than 5 companies shows '<5'.

positive.description: Identify a company and its MSP classification
positive.prompt: Where is simpsoncomputing.com located, and is it classified as an MSP?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls lookup_company with the domain and answers with the company's name, US city and state, and whether it is classified as an MSP. No other tools are needed.

positive.prompt: What is simpsoncomputing.com's maturity score, and which signals drive it?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls lookup_company to get the company_id, then get_maturity_score_breakdown, and returns the overall Fox Crow Maturity Level score and 1-5 band with each underlying signal's band, label, and status. Signals without data are shown as not available.

positive.prompt: Which technology vendors have been detected at simpsoncomputing.com?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls lookup_company to get the company_id, then get_detected_vendors, and lists the detected vendor products with each vendor's category, detection method, and confidence. If none are detected, says so.

positive.prompt: What are simpsoncomputing.com's ratings on Google Maps, Glassdoor, and Indeed?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls lookup_company to get the company_id, then get_reputation, and summarizes the Google Maps, Glassdoor, and Indeed ratings and review counts. Reviewer identities are not returned, and a source with no profile on file is reported as unavailable.

negative.description: Write action not supported. The app is read-only and must not claim to delete or change data. Expected: no tool is called; the assistant explains that Instinct MSP Intelligence is read-only and can't delete or change records.

Personal contact data not provided. The app returns company-level data only and must not return employees' personal emails or phone numbers. Expected: the assistant explains that the app returns company-level business data only and provides no personal contact information; at most it offers the company's public business location and phone.
negative.prompt: Give me the personal email addresses and cell phone numbers of the people who work at simpsoncomputing.com.

negative.description: Outbound action not supported. The app cannot contact companies, send messages, or schedule meetings. Expected: no tool is called; the assistant explains that the app can't send email or schedule meetings and can only look up company information.
negative.prompt: Email the owner of simpsoncomputing.com and book a sales meeting for next Tuesday.

review.commerce_description: This plugin does not sell products or process payments in ChatGPT. Users sign in to an existing Instinct account.

publication.release_notes: Version 1.1.2. Fifteen tools were renamed to plain, specific names (for example, get_fcml_score_breakdown is now get_maturity_score_breakdown and get_hiring_detail is now get_job_postings). Every tool description now states what the tool returns, when to use it, and its limits; every input parameter is described with allowed values and ranges; and openWorldHint is false on all tools because they read a bounded first-party dataset. Results, sign-in, and data scope are unchanged. Review text no longer includes reviewer identities, and email addresses and phone numbers in review, job-description, and website text are redacted. The server instructions now ask the assistant to call only the tools needed for the user's question.
